Indigenous Creativity – Indigenous ways of knowing have been misunderstood and oppressed throughout the Western colonial project, yet Indigenous people continue advancing diverse creative practices based on accountability to all relations in a process of becoming more human. Read at least two (any two) of the following excerpts from the work of Gregory Cajete ( pp.2-5 and 15-55 ), Leanne B. Simpson ( pp. 198-210 ), Mavhunga ( introduction ), or Joe Sheridan on the Haudenosaunee Imagination and Ecology of the Sacred , and answer the question: how is creative practice part of becoming more human?
Scientific Eyes – Science goes hand in hand with creative thinking, as scientists must figure out how to explain/theorize their empirical observations. Read Barry Bickmore's piece " Creativity In Science " – you do not need to complete the quiz or check out the additional resources. Instead, write your essay as a constructive critique / response to the information and insights presented by Bickmore, making explicit links to what you are learning in class while incorporating ideas from: Alan Sears and James Cairns's chapter " But How Do You Know ?" and Root-Bernstein's chapter 3 " Observing ." Your essay should answer the question: how is creative thinking part of advancing a scientific understanding of the world, through combining observation and theory?
Open topic – Propose another case study topic of interest to you; make sure it includes at least two new relevant readings and poses a question that you can answer in a 1000-1500 word essay, drawing on your learning in the course. Please email me by Oct 9 to confirm this option works for you.
